"A seven year affair is shown from the end back to the start. A play in reverse chronology (the scenes move from later years to earlier years). The talk is short, and the pain sits in what is not said."
items.explanation: 'Betrayal' (1978) is a prominent drama by Harold Pinter. A seven year affair is shown from the end back to the start. A play in reverse chronology (the scenes move from later years to earlier years). The talk is short, and the pain sits in what is not said..

items.title: Quiz Q#747 · Jacques Derrida
items.meta: Post-War, Postmodern & Contemporary Era · Jacques Derrida
items.stem: In which work by Jacques Derrida does the character Jacques Derrida (The philosopher who argues for a new study of writing) appear?
items.explanation: The character Jacques Derrida (The philosopher who argues for a new study of writing) appears in Jacques Derrida's Of Grammatology (1967).

items.title: Quiz Q#748 · Jacques Derrida
items.meta: Post-War, Postmodern & Contemporary Era · Jacques Derrida
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following line?
"There is nothing outside the text."
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Jacques Derrida's Of Grammatology (1967).

items.title: Quiz Q#749 · Jacques Derrida
items.meta: Post-War, Postmodern & Contemporary Era · Jacques Derrida
items.stem:
Which literary theory by Jacques Derrida (1967) is characterized by the following thematic premise and narrative design?
"A theory book that says writing is not a mere copy of speech."
items.explanation: 'Of Grammatology' (1967) is a prominent literary theory by Jacques Derrida. A theory book that says writing is not a mere copy of speech..

items.title: Quiz Q#750 · Jacques Derrida
items.meta: Post-War, Postmodern & Contemporary Era · Jacques Derrida
items.stem: In which work by Jacques Derrida does the character Jacques Derrida (The essayist who reads other thinkers against their own claims) appear?
items.explanation: The character Jacques Derrida (The essayist who reads other thinkers against their own claims) appears in Jacques Derrida's Writing and Difference (1967).
